original_cells: `run_investigation` stores `aoi["polygon"]` (not `geojson`) in `run_state["aoi"]`. On any `apply_what_if` call (`mode`, `flare_guard`, `focus_period`, `persona`), `req = {**run_state["aoi"], **opts}` lacks `"geojson"`, so `parse_custom_aoi` ignores `polygon`, replaces the user's polygon (or uploaded CSV bbox) with `_square_ring(lat, lon, radius_km)`, alters `area_km2` (via rounded `radius_km`), changes `aoi_id`, re-seeds RNG, and mutates `verdict_sha256`.

Accept `spec.get("polygon")` directly in `parse_custom_aoi` (preserving explicit `aoi_id`, `name`, `country`, `biome` when `is_uploaded_csv`/`is_custom` is passed in `apply_what_if`), and hash the canonical polygon vertex ring via SHA-256 so geometry round-trips losslessly.
disposition: Full geometry and sources survive all experiments

original_cells: `decide()` inspects `calendar["cells"]` to detect `early_season_onset` (`prev_cell`). `build_receipt()` omits `cells` and `verify.py:55` hardcodes `"cells": []`. Whenever `early_season_onset` triggers (reproduced on `AOI-AMZ 2023-05`, `AOI-CAL 2021-10`, `AOI-NSW 2004-03`, `AOI-MIO 2006-09`), `verify.py` fails to re-derive the finding and falsely rejects FireTrace's own valid receipt as `TAMPERED` (`exit 1`).

Include `prev_month_z_robust` / `prev_month_name` (or compact observed `cells` / `focus_context`) inside `calendar["focus_comparison"]` (which is already serialized in `receipt.json` and cross-checked against `Q7`) so `decide()` is 100% self-contained without scanning `calendar["cells"]`, OR embed `cells` and verify `sha256_of(cells) == cells_sha256` in `verify.py`. Doing BOTH makes `verify.py` airtight!
disposition: V2 embeds full calendar; verifier rederives all rule context; v1 frozen with narrower scope

original_cells: `apply_what_if(..., "focus_to_median", True)` mutates `updated["calendar"]["focus_comparison"]["value"]` in-place on a deepcopy without updating `updated["queries"]` (`Q6.rows[0].focus_value` and `Q6.sha256` or `Q4`). Downloading `receipt.json` after clicking that UI counterfactual button fails `verify.py` with `TAMPERED: Q6 focus_value disagrees with calendar_summary.focus_comparison.value`.
Rebuild `queries` via `_build_query_tables(...)` (and avoid in-place mutation) inside the `focus_to_median` branch so `Q4`/`Q6` hashes and `calendar_summary` remain cryptographically synchronized.
disposition: Median is explicit new metric scenario; queries/calendar/receipt rebuilt; observed input unchanged

original_cells: `raw_bytes = await file.read()` reads arbitrary-sized multipart uploads into memory before checking size. A multi-hundred-MB upload exhausts server memory.

Enforce a strict byte cap (e.g., `MAX_CSV_BYTES = 10 * 1024 * 1024` = 10 MB) via chunked/bounded read `await file.read(MAX_CSV_BYTES + 1)`, returning HTTP `413` or `422` if exceeded, and reject NUL bytes / binary payloads cleanly.
disposition: Bounded streamed multipart envelope and file read

original_cells: `api.py` uses untyped `dict[str, Any] = Body(...)` and only catches `ValueError`. Sending `focus_month=13` raises unhandled `IndexError` at `MONTH_NAMES[focus_month - 1]` (`agents.py:436`); `focus_month=0` or `-1` wraps via Python negative indexing to `"Dec"` in trace while `calendar_engine.py:255` clamps to `"Jan"`; `year_start=null` or `focus_period=null` / `[2026]` raises unhandled `TypeError`/`IndexError` (HTTP 500).

Validate all request bodies via strict Pydantic models (or explicit boundary validators raising `ValueError` → HTTP 422): enforce `2000 <= year_start <= year_end <= 2026`, `1 <= focus_month <= 12`, `year_start <= focus_year <= year_end`, valid `mode`, `confidence_min`, `persona`, and `focus_period` 2-tuple `[year, month]`.
disposition: Typed strict analysis/what-if contracts and controlled errors

original_cells: `custom_id` (`CUSTOM-xxxx`) and CSV `aoi_id` (`CSV-xxxx`) use Python's platform/version-dependent `hash(...) % 10000`. Two distinct polygons with the same rounded centroid & area collide onto the same `aoi_id`, RNG `_seed_for`, and `run_id`. Furthermore, two different uploaded CSVs with the same `(len(rows), round(c_lat, 2), round(c_lon, 2))` get the exact same `run_id`, overwriting each other in `RUNS` because `run_id` hashes only `aoi_id` + `options`, not raw CSV digest or polygon coordinates!

Replace all `hash(...)` calls with `sha256_of(...)` over canonicalized polygon coordinates (for custom AOIs) and raw normalized record digest (for uploaded CSVs), and include geometry/dataset digest in `_seed_for` and `run_id`.
disposition: SHA-256 canonical geometry/data/options/code/reference identity; immutable collision checks

original_cells: Two logic bugs in `early_season_onset`: (1) When `focus["month"] == 1` (Jan), `prev_mo = 12` looks up `c["year"] == focus["year"] and c["month"] == 12` (**Dec of the SAME year, 11 months in the future!**) instead of `focus["year"] - 1`; (2) Only checking `not focus["is_peak_season"]` causes post-peak autumn decay months immediately following peak season (`AOI-CAL` Oct, `AOI-NSW` Mar, `AOI-MIO` Sep) to be mislabelled `"early fire-season onset"`.

Look up `(focus["year"] - 1, 12)` when `focus["month"] == 1`, and verify that `focus["month"]` is genuinely **pre-peak** (e.g., `next_mo in peak_months` or rising climatological slope toward peak, distinguishing `early_season_onset` from `late_season_persistence`).
disposition: Previous December uses previous year; onset restricted to two pre-onset months

original_cells: `"z_before": round(float(med_cal["focus_comparison"]["z_robust"] if False else alt_cal["focus_comparison"]["z_robust"]), 2)` contains leftover `if False` dead code and assigns `alt_cal` (`z_after`!) to `z_before` (`6.08` instead of `7.50` on `AOI-AMZ`).

Compute `z_before` from the active base calendar (`active_cal["focus_comparison"]["z_robust"]`) and also expose `z_after` (`alt_cal["focus_comparison"]["z_robust"]`) on all 3 counterfactual experiments.
disposition: Before/after metrics computed from correct active/alternate calendars; removed dead branch

original_cells: `verify.py` checks Q0–Q8 internal row hashes and `Q6.focus_value == fc.value`, but NEVER verifies `calendar_summary.cells_sha256` and NEVER cross-checks `Q0` (`aoi_id`, `lat`, `lon`), `Q3` (`calibrated_kappa`), `Q4` (`focus_night_share`), `Q5` (`flare_contamination_share`), `Q6` (`hist_median`, `hist_p95`, `z_robust`), `Q7` (`peak_months`), or `Q8` (`trend_slope_per_decade`, `bias_reduction_pct`) against `evidence`. An attacker can forge `Q0`–`Q5`/`Q7`–`Q8` + their row `sha256`s inside `receipt.json` without `verify.py` noticing!
Cross-check all Q0–Q8 summary metrics against `aoi`, `calendar_summary`, and `sensor_calibration_audit` (and verify `cells_sha256` if `cells` are included or via a binding receipt manifest hash).
disposition: All nine required queries/counts/hashes and evidence/decision relationships verified; unsigned scope explicit

original_cells: `parse_custom_aoi` accepts: (a) polygons with unlimited vertices (500k-vertex polygon causes O(N·V) CPU DoS in `point_in_polygon`); (b) collinear/zero-area degenerate polygons (`[[0,0],[1,1],[2,2],[0,0]]`); (c) self-intersecting bow-tie polygons; (d) non-list/short coordinates `[10]` raising 500 `IndexError`/`TypeError`; (e) concave C-polygons where centroid `(aoi["lat"], aoi["lon"])` lies outside the polygon, yet `generate_firms_records` falls back to `(cx, cy) = centroid` outside the user's AOI!

Enforce vertex count bounds (`4 <= len(ring) <= 2000`), validate 2-element finite `[lon, lat]` pairs, reject zero-area (`polygon_area_km2 <= 0.01`), self-intersecting, or antimeridian-spanning (`lon_max - lon_min > 180`) rings with clear HTTP 422 errors, and guarantee interior fallback points via vertex/ear midpoint sampling.
disposition: Strict bounded full geometry with holes/components; invalid rings rejected, observations remain in AOI

original_cells: > 177°`) generates vertices outside `[-90, 90]` / `[-180, 180]`; (2) `parse_uploaded_csv` neither filters out-of-bounds rows (`lat=999`) before computing `min`/`max` bbox nor clamps `pad_lat`/`pad_lon` to `[-90, 90]`/`[-180, 180]`, causing valid high-latitude/Pacific CSV uploads or CSVs with 1 corrupt row to crash `parse_custom_aoi` with HTTP 422; (3) CSVs where all rows have invalid `acq_date` pass `parse_uploaded_csv` (`rows` appended before date parse at `:619-627`).

Clamp `_square_ring` and CSV padded bbox rings to `[-90.0, 90.0]` and `[-180.0, 180.0]`; validate `-90 <= lat <= 90`, `-180 <= lon <= 180`, and valid ISO `acq_date` inside `parse_uploaded_csv` (tracking `skipped_invalid_rows` cleanly and rejecting CSVs with 0 valid FIRMS rows).
disposition: Dateline/polar bounds and geometry identity; CSV focus follows latest valid row

original_cells: `package_zip` uses `zf.writestr("filename", ...)` which stamps `time.localtime()` into every `ZipInfo.date_time` header, and `evidence.json` embeds `trace[*].timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc)`. Calling `/runs/{run_id}/package` twice produces non-identical `.zip` bytes. Also `csv.DictWriter` emits `\r\n` while JSON/MD emit `\n`.

Write ZIP entries using deterministic `ZipInfo(filename, date_time=(2026, 11, 14, 0, 0, 0))` with fixed `compress_type=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED` and `external_attr=0o644 << 16`, normalize CSV `lineterminator="\n"`, and keep `verdict_sha256` / `receipt.json` completely timestamp-free (or use deterministic logical step sequence in receipts).
disposition: Fixed reference trace and sorted ZIP epoch/permissions/compression; byte equality

original_cells: Selecting a preset pill (e.g., `AOI-AMZ`) fills `#in-lat`/`#in-lon`/`#in-radius`, but submitting `#query-form` ("Analyze Region") after changing only year/month/confidence omits `aoi_id`, silently converting preset `AOI-AMZ` (`CRITICAL_ANOMALY`) into synthetic `Custom AOI` (`CUSTOM-8824`, `NOMINAL_REGIME`) while leaving the `AOI-AMZ` pill highlighted as `.active`!
Track `state.selectedPresetId`; clear it only when `#in-lat`, `#in-lon`, or `#in-radius` changes from the preset's coordinates, and include `aoi_id` in `#query-form` submit when unchanged.
disposition: Source-preserving option form uses retained snapshot; no accidental preset-to-custom conversion

original_cells: `is_observed = not (yr == 2026 and mo == 12)` is hardcoded globally: (a) uploaded FIRMS CSVs containing December 2026 rows silently have all Dec 2026 detections zeroed out; (b) uploaded CSVs ending in e.g. 2023 falsely mark 2024–Nov 2026 as observed `0.0` fire months; (c) requesting `focus_year=2026, focus_month=12` leaves `options.focus_month = 12` while `calendar.focus_month = 11`.

For uploaded CSVs, derive observed window from actual dataset coverage (or `year_start..year_end`); synchronize `options["focus_year"]`/`options["focus_month"]` with effective focus period or reject unobserved focus months cleanly.
disposition: Missing/records_only/complete coverage; explicit focus preserved, December CSV not discarded

original_cells: `night_share = round(b["night_hhe"] / denom_metric, 4)` divides unrounded `b["night_hhe"]` by already-rounded `hhe_total = round(b["hhe"], 2)`. When 100% of detections are nocturnal and `b["hhe"]` rounds down (e.g., `1.234 -> 1.23`), `night_share` exceeds `1.0` (`100.33%`).
Compute `night_share = min(1.0, max(0.0, round(b["night_hhe"] / b["hhe"], 4)))` using unrounded `b["hhe"] > 0` before display rounding.
disposition: Known D/N share computed from unrounded contributions and bounded by its denominator

original_cells: Three harmonization defects: (1) `overpass_dedup_factor` is computed (`:125`) and exported, **never used** in `modis_w`/`viirs_w`/`hhe`; (2) `_pearson_r2(xs, ys)` where `ys = kappa * V_m` is algebraically invariant to scalar `kappa > 0`, masking scale/step errors; (3) In `m_val > 0 and v_val > 0` months (`:253-255`), `target_hhe / raw_sum_contrib` simplifies identically to `0.5`, halving standalone morning Terra MODIS-only cells relative to pre-2012 months.

Incorporate constellation-era normalization (S-NPP 2012+, S-NPP+NOAA-20 2018+, +NOAA-21 2023+), report both Pearson $r^2$ and 1:1 calibration skill ($R^2_{\text{1:1}}$ / MAE), and weight co-detected vs single-sensor cells physically while preserving `judge.py` invariants.
disposition: Unique observation revisions, satellite family mean occupancy; R2 separate from efficiency/RMSE. Monthly half-blend is an explicit index convention, not physical equivalence

original_cells: Pre-2012 (`yr < 2012`), `elif not modis_emitted:` forces 100% of small agricultural fires to emit a MODIS record anyway, whereas post-2012 (`yr >= 2012`) 35% of agricultural fires omit MODIS. This creates an artificial `-28%` drop in raw MODIS counts in 2012 on `AOI-MEK`, explaining why harmonized `AOI-MEK` jumps `-29.8%` in 2012!

Audit carefully: any tweak to `generate_firms_records` will change `AOI-AMZ`/`AOI-MEK`/`AOI-FLR` seals in `output_examples/*.json`. Document or refine only if regenerating `output_examples/*.json` and keeping all 12 `BENCH_CASES` + 7 `judge.py` claims green!
disposition: Removed forced pre-2012 MODIS detection; availability and omission applied consistently

original_cells: Uses flat-Earth `atan2(cross_km, altitude_km)` instead of spherical-Earth viewing zenith angle (underestimating swath-edge VZA by ~8–10° and overestimating observer elevation), assigns different `day_lst_hour` (`13.50`, `13.42`, `13.33`) instead of same-plane `13:30` LST along-track phase separation for JPSS satellites, and omits off-nadir bow-tie pixel area growth (`scan × track` km²).

Compute true spherical Earth central angle $\psi = d / R_E$, nadir angle $\eta$, local Viewing Zenith Angle $\text{VZA} = \arcsin(\frac{R_E+h}{R_E}\sin\eta)$, observer elevation $90^\circ - \text{VZA}$, ascending/descending pass node, and instantaneous pixel footprint `effective_pixel_km2`!
disposition: Spherical viewing geometry, bounded schematic nominal solar phase; footprint metadata/defaults explicit. No ephemeris or bow-tie correction claimed

original_cells: Security (RFC 5545 Control Char & CSV Formula Injection)

(1) `_ics_escape` escapes `\`, `;`, `,`, `\n` but leaves `\r` and control chars unstripped, breaking RFC 5545 line grammar if `aoi["name"]` contains `\r`; (2) CSV exports do not neutralize leading spreadsheet formula triggers (`=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, `\t`, `\r`) on string fields (`aoi_id` or user-derived strings) and lack RFC 5545 75-octet line folding.
Normalize `\r\n`/`\r` → `\n` and strip control chars before `_ics_escape` (plus optional RFC 5545 75-octet folding), and sanitize leading formula characters on untrusted string cells in CSV exports.
disposition: CSV formula neutralization and RFC5545 control normalization/UTF8 folding

original_cells: (1) `export_hotspots_csv` slices `rows[:5000]` chronologically from year 2000, dropping 2026 focus-year hotspots on dense runs (contradicting its own comment on `:25`), and includes excluded static flare rows (`hhe=0.0`) without exporting `include_in_calendar`; (2) `export_hotspots_geojson` (`limit=600`) reads `map_hotspots` first (hard-capped at 450 in `agents.py:514`), ignoring `limit > 450`.

Export `include_in_calendar` in `hotspots.csv`, prioritize focus-year events or raise default limit cleanly so all benchmark runs export 100% of events, and slice `_hotspots_all` properly in `export_hotspots_geojson` when `limit > len(map_hotspots)`.
disposition: Complete retained events by default, explicit inclusion/missing flags; labeled optional previews only

original_cells: Global `RUNS` dict has no lock (`threading.Lock`), uses FIFO eviction instead of LRU (`OrderedDict`), and `what_if` overwrites `RUNS[run_id]` in place even though `options` changed (mutating shared run state across browser tabs or previously downloaded URLs).

Guard `RUNS` with an `OrderedDict` + `threading.Lock` LRU cache; either assign derived `run_id` per distinct `(aoi, options)` state (while keeping old `run_id` cached!) or preserve immutable run snapshots.
disposition: Copy-in/out locked bounded LRU and new content IDs for experiments

original_cells: `clean_float(raw.get("frp"), 12.0) or 0.0` silently invents `12.0 MW` when `frp` is missing/null in an uploaded CSV (`None` → default `12.0`), inflating radiative power and misclassifying missing-FRP daytime fires, and `clean_float(...) or fallback` conflates legitimate `0.0` with `None`.
Use explicit `is None` checks instead of truthiness `or`, and default missing `frp` conservatively (e.g. `0.0` or sensor-specific nominal floor) rather than `12.0 MW`.
disposition: No invented FRP/temperature; valid zero preserved; missing flags exported

original_cells: (1) Comment at `harmonize.py:65` promises `>= 8 distinct months in any year or >= 14 total months at same cell`, while `:81` omits the multi-year persistence check (missing flares in short 2-year CSVs with 7 months/yr); (2) `harmonize.py:210` fits overlap over `2012..2024` while `schema_mapping.py:224` & `MAPPING_MANIFESTO.md:46` say `2012–2025`.
Implement multi-year cell persistence (`len(ym_set) >= 14` when dataset spans $\ge 2$ years) and align overlap window documentation & code consistently.
disposition: Multi-year persistence is only a descriptive flag; supplied types distinct; shared overlap docs2012-2024

original_cells: Maintainability / Coding Standards (Divergent Change & Long Functions)

`app.js` (899 lines) breaches the 800-line soft ceiling. Several Python functions exceed the 50-line guideline: `harmonize_records` (`harmonize.py:43-339`, **297 lines!**), `build_burning_calendar` (`calendar_engine.py:61-328`, **268 lines!**), `generate_firms_records` (`datasets.py:398-596`, **199 lines!**), `run_investigation` (`agents.py:398-553`, **156 lines!**), `decide` (`rules.py:30-170`, **141 lines!**), `_compute_what_ifs` (`agents.py:294-395`, **102 lines!**), `parse_custom_aoi` (`datasets.py:305-390`, **86 lines!**).

Decompose giant functions into focused <50-line pure helpers (e.g. `_detect_persistent_flares`, `_cluster_cell_events`, `_fit_overlap_bridge`, `_compute_step_audit` in `harmonize.py`; modular ES modules or split view renderers for frontend).
disposition: Frontend split into focused modules; geometry/stats/observations/evidence/state/store extracted. Remaining cohesive algorithm functions retained; survey line ceilings were advisory, not repo rules
verification: full regression suite; independent Standards review

original_cells: `requirements.txt` includes 4 unused heavy libraries (`numpy`, `pandas`, `requests`, `cryptography`), omits test runner `pytest`, and `run.py:13` hard-crashes if `python-dotenv` isn't installed even when no `.env` file is needed. Host Python currently lacks `fastapi`, `python-dotenv`, and `pytest`.

Install required packages in workspace Python/venv; make `dotenv` optional (`try: from dotenv import load_dotenv except ImportError: ...`) or ensure `requirements.txt` is lean, accurate, and matches `README.md` setup instructions.
disposition: Pinned minimal runtime plus dev browser dependency; stdlib unittest, multipart declared; fresh venv installed
verification: fresh install and pip check; full suite; smoke_test.py

Return explicit 404/422 on unknown `aoi_id` in `/api/passes` and document all endpoints accurately in `README.md` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

original_cells: **Uncaught Promise Rejections & Invisible Error Banner**: `loadReceiptJson()` (`:826`), `loadManifesto()` (`:836`), and `runBenchSuite()` (`:873`) have **no `catch` handler**, throwing uncaught Promise rejections on HTTP/network errors. `#global-error` lives inside `#control-deck`, which is `hidden` on `#/manifesto` and `#/bench` (`:116`). `apiJSON` (`:62`) & `handleCsvUpload` (`:288-289`) format FastAPI 422 array `detail` as `"[object Object]"`, and `handleCsvUpload` lacks `.json().catch(...)`.
